_comment: ff_fuel (brief D1, issues #32 and #37, patches/ff_fuel/): the flex-fuel
state block plus the stock signals the E0 equivalence run compares.
patches/ff_fuel/test/procedure.md is the full bench procedure; this file
is only the variable list it needs.
Addresses of the ff_* variables come from patches/ff_fuel/patch.json
build.ram (0x7FFB00, 0x100 B) plus the offsets documented in
patches/ff_fuel/src/ff_state.h.  READ THEM OUT OF patch.json, not out of
this file, the day the block moves:
python3 logging/med9log.py log --session logging/sessions/ff_fuel.json \
--patch patches/ff_fuel/patch.json --bus gs_usb:0 --seconds 120 \
-o logs/2026-xx-xx_ff_fuel.csv
resolves every patch_offset against build.ram and overrides the addresses
below.
Checks, in order (procedure.md sections 2-5):
1. ff_magic == 0x46463031 ('FF01') and ff_length == 64.  If they are
zero the hook never ran: look at ff_src_seen first.
2. ff_src_seen answers scheduler.md 11.7 in one sample: 1 = only the
task-set-A hook (0x432940) fires, 2 = only the set-B hook (0x12067C),
3 = both (which the OS should make impossible).  ff_src_owner is the
one that actually ticks.
3. ff_ticks rises by about 100 per second (the raster is 10 ms, not
100 ms - C4, issue #44).  It must track raster_setA_10ms_count or
raster_setB_10ms_count 1:1, whichever set is live.
4. With no Pico on the bus: ff_mode == 3 (FAULT), ff_e_filt == 0 and
ff_f_q10 == 1024.  1024 is the bit-identical-to-stock value, so this
is also the E0 equivalence condition.
5. With the Pico running: ff_frames rises, ff_mode == 1 (OK),
ff_e_filt follows the frame at no more than 2 %/s, ff_f_q10 follows
ff_F_curve, and ff_rk_calls rises with engine speed (it counts
segments, not raster activations).
Record the same variables on the STOCK image first: that baseline and the
ff_fuel log are what tools/logcmp.py compares with
patches/ff_fuel/test/tolerance.json.

vars.name: ff_magic
vars.notes: 0x46463031 = 1179599921 once ff_state_init() has run

vars.name: ff_length
vars.notes: 64; together with the magic and the csum it is the cold-start marker

vars.name: ff_csum
vars.notes: bit-complement of the 16-bit byte sum of +0x08..+0x27

vars.name: ff_e_filt
vars.notes: filtered ethanol, 1/16 % per LSB, 0..1600 counts

vars.name: ff_f_q10
vars.notes: the fuel mass factor the rk hook applies; 1024 = 1.000 = stock

vars.name: ff_mode
vars.notes: 0 INIT, 1 OK, 2 HOLD, 3 FAULT, 4 OFF, 5 OVERRIDE

vars.name: ff_status
vars.notes: byte 7 of the last frame: 0 OK, 1 fault, 2 contaminated, 3 not ready; 255 = no frame yet

vars.name: ff_e_raw
vars.notes: byte 0 of the last frame, unfiltered

vars.name: ff_t_fuel
vars.notes: byte 1 of the last frame, degC + 40

vars.name: ff_frame_ctr
vars.notes: byte 3 of the last frame; frozen for 3 frames -> FAULT

vars.name: ff_fw_ver
vars.notes: byte 6 of the last frame: the Pico firmware version

vars.name: ff_cal_mode
vars.notes: ff_mode as read from FFCAL001: 0 off, 1 normal, 2 bench override

vars.name: ff_cal_ok
vars.notes: 1 = FFCAL001 magic, version, length and checksum all accepted

vars.name: ff_age_ticks
vars.notes: activations since the last good frame; x ff_tick_ms = ms

vars.name: ff_hold_ticks
vars.notes: activations left of the 60 s FAULT hold; 6000 at entry

vars.name: ff_frames
vars.notes: good frames since power-up, saturating; +10/s with the Pico running

vars.name: ff_faults
vars.notes: FAULT entries since power-up; 1 before the first frame arrives is normal

vars.name: ff_stall
vars.notes: consecutive frames with an unchanged rolling counter

vars.name: ff_src_owner
vars.notes: 1 = the task-set-A hook (0x432940) ticks, 2 = the set-B hook (0x12067C)

vars.name: ff_src_seen
vars.notes: bit0 set A has fired, bit1 set B has fired. This one sample answers scheduler.md 11.7

vars.name: ff_src_foreign
vars.notes: consecutive calls from the non-owner hook; must stay 0 in normal running

vars.name: ff_ticks
vars.notes: periodic activations since power-up; +100/s, tracks the live 10 ms raster counter 1:1

vars.name: ff_e_key
vars.notes: the value the FAULT decay aims at; 0 (E0) until brief D2 loads it from EEPROM block 8

vars.name: ff_e_frac
vars.notes: sub-count of ff_e_filt, 1/1024 of a 1/16 % count; carries the 0.32-count slew step

vars.name: ff_rk_calls
vars.notes: segment-task invocations of the rk hook; rises with engine speed, 0 with the engine off

vars.name: ff_diag_e_pct
vars.notes: reserved for brief D2 (#33); stays 0 with the MVP flashed

vars.name: ff_diag_f_pct
vars.notes: reserved for brief D2 (#33); stays 0 with the MVP flashed

vars.name: raster_setA_10ms_count
vars.notes: set A 10 ms epilogue; +100/s if set A is live

vars.name: raster_setB_10ms_count
vars.notes: set B 10 ms epilogue; +100/s if set B is live

vars.name: raster_setB_1ms_count
vars.notes: +1000/s; the time reference for every slope in this session

vars.name: rk_fuel_mass
vars.notes: the cell the rk hook scales. Stock vs patched at E0 must be identical sample for sample

vars.name: dwi_inj_angle
vars.notes: the injection window signal: rk x 1.5 raises this by ~50 %

vars.name: prist_w
vars.notes: must stay above 13 bar (rail.md section 14) or three limp-home limits arm at once

vars.name: can_rx_spare0_b0
vars.notes: byte 0 of the raw frame in can_rx_shadow slot 15: proves reception independently of our state machine

vars.name: can_rx_spare0_ctr
vars.notes: byte 3, the rolling counter, straight out of the driver shadow
